S18.title: The Lighthouse. Eric and the Unsent Postcard

paragraphs.S18.C000.P000: Eric was waiting by the door with two thermoses instead of a map. One was his, with a peeling sticker; the other belonged to the guesthouse.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P001: “Tea in one,” he said. “Tea in the other too. I'm not a talented enough date organiser.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P002: He said the word “date” calmly, but checked her face. Alice took the second thermos.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P003: “A good start. At least you didn't promise me a sunrise at nine in the evening.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P005: The wind was weaker behind the houses than at the lagoon, but on the open stretch the cold immediately found the gap between her scarf and collar. They followed the town path to the harbour. Light along the shore flickered behind moored boats; farther out, the dark water made the distance deceptive. Eric suggested stopping by the railing instead of walking on the wet rocks.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P006: “Is that a professional habit?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P007: “Today it's a wish to keep your shoes intact. We can turn back too.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P009: He handed her the thermos. She poured the tea herself, holding the lid in her palm. Eric's sleeves were wet: while everyone else had dried their clothes, he had forgotten his own jacket. Alice reminded him. He looked at the fabric with genuine surprise.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P010: “The route specialist has an uninspected stretch,” she said.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P011: “Now you can write an honest review.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P012: They watched the lighthouse beam. Alice remembered how he had gone quiet that morning when she asked to stay at the lagoon for ten more minutes. At the time, she had thought he considered the request a whim.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P013: “Were you angry about the stop?” she asked.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P014: Eric leaned on the cold railing.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P015: “I was counting the time. I wasn't angry with you. But I didn't say that, and I suppose it looked the same.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P016: “Yes. I was already preparing to argue.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P017: “You can argue now too. Sometimes I choose the short answer because the long one sounds like an excuse.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P018: She liked that he did not immediately explain her feeling to her. She told him how, as a child, she had been afraid of falling behind on a tour: her mother walked quickly, while Alice kept finding stones and signs she wanted to read. Eric listened without turning the memory into a lesson about the right pace.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P019: “And you?” she asked. “Where do you hurry when no one is paying you to plan a route?”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P020: “Home,” he answered after a pause. “Although in recent years ‘home’ has turned out to be a different address every time.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P021: He had come here for one season and stayed for several. He liked showing people places, but was tired of being the person who always knew the answer to the next question. Outside work he had a few friends, old music in the car, and a box of things he had never fully unpacked. Alice could have asked why he stayed. Instead she asked whether the box held anything he missed.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P022: “My grandfather's postcards. He sent them from towns where almost nothing happened. On each one he wrote one new word and one very boring detail. That way I knew he had really been there.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P023: Eric took a folded postcard from his pocket, bought today at the guesthouse desk. On the front was a boat photographed so close that the shore did not enter the frame. The back was still blank.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P024: “I wanted to write to my sister,” he said. “‘Everything is going according to plan.’ I haven't been able to for twenty minutes.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P026: He turned the postcard toward the light from his phone, but did not ask her to finish it for him.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P027: “I wanted you to come out with me. And I didn't know how to suggest it without turning the walk into part of a schedule.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P028: Alice felt pleased and wary at the same time. She had enough experience to know that admitting a desire was not an agreement about tomorrow. She said it more simply.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P029: “I came out because I wanted to too. Today. I can't answer for tomorrow.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P031: They quietly shared the rest of the tea. Music drifted from the open door of a small place by the harbour—an old song Alice had heard in the car and had not managed to ask the name of. Eric recognised the first notes and, to her surprise, sang a few words. His voice was low and not especially accurate.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P033: “No. I just don't feel embarrassed by this song.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P034: His sister used to play it while they cleaned their first shared home: one of them held a box, the other invariably dropped it on the floor and started dancing. In that memory Eric was a younger brother, not a man who always had the car key and a backup route. Alice asked him to show her what his sister called dancing. He set the empty thermos on a dry bench and held out his hand. She adjusted her scarf and stepped closer herself.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P035: Eric took two steps to the side, Alice tried to copy him, and they both stopped when people came out of the place. It was not the mistake that made them laugh, but Eric's serious face as he tried to remember a third move. Alice invented one of her own and pulled him along. The song ended before they produced anything resembling a dance.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P036: “Your sister does it better?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P037: “She claims she does. You can check one day, if you meet her.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P038: He did not say it as an invitation into a ready-made future. Alice heard only a possibility that felt pleasant for a second. She returned the thermos, and they walked on without the music.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P039: On the way back, they noticed that one of the town signs had been turned by the wind. Its arrow pointed toward wet rocks, while the lit pavement went around a warehouse. Eric took out the map, but Alice stopped him:
paragraphs.S18.C000.P040: “There's the street name on that door. Let's check with our feet; the crossroads are two minutes away.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P041: She walked onto the pavement first. The detour led to the right place. Eric photographed the sign for the guesthouse owner, who had been giving guests that landmark in the morning. Alice noticed her reflection at the edge of the frame; he retook the picture without her and sent the owner a short message. A few minutes later, a thank-you arrived with a promise to check the sign in the morning.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P042: “We came out for tea and already fixed the route,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S18.C000.P043: “You fixed the route. I know how to send photographs.”
paragraphs.S18.C000.P044: By the railing, she handed him the thermos lid. Their fingers lingered on the same edge of metal. Eric asked:
paragraphs.S18.C000.P046: Alice placed the lid on the railing and looked at him before answering. The lighthouse beam slid across the water and moved on.

S18.C001.title: Choice S18-C1 — Closeness by the railing

paragraphs.S18.C002.P000: “Yes,” Alice said. “Just not as a route item.”
paragraphs.S18.C002.P001: “I don't have a column for that.”
paragraphs.S18.C002.P002: He did not pull her toward him; she took the step herself. The kiss was brief because of the cold air and unexpectedly warm because afterward no one hurried to call it the beginning of something large. Alice touched his wet sleeve.
paragraphs.S18.C002.P003: “You really need to dry that jacket.”
paragraphs.S18.C002.P004: “That's my best plan for the rest of the night.”
paragraphs.S18.C002.P005: They laughed and walked back beside each other, without automatically holding hands.

paragraphs.S18.C003.P000: “I feel good here,” Alice said. “I don't need a kiss yet.”
paragraphs.S18.C003.P001: Eric moved his hand from the railing so she would not be caught between his hand and the metal.
paragraphs.S18.C003.P004: “I know. And I'm still glad you stayed.”
paragraphs.S18.C003.P005: On the way back, he asked what song to play in the car tomorrow. Alice chose the one whose name he had once failed to tell her. Their argument about music lasted all the way to the house.

S18.C004.title: C. Ask to end the walk

paragraphs.S18.C004.P000: “I want to go back,” Alice said. “We've talked more than I expected.”
paragraphs.S18.C004.P001: Eric closed the thermos at once.
paragraphs.S18.C004.P002: “Let's go. I can walk you to the house and say goodnight there.”
paragraphs.S18.C004.P004: He did not ask whether he had ruined everything with a word. At the guesthouse, Alice said she had liked hearing about his postcards. Eric thanked her and went to dry his jacket. Nothing promised and nothing owed remained by the door.

paragraphs.S18.C005.P000: In her room, Alice wrote not “lighthouse—romance” but: “When I was asked, I was able to answer at once.”
paragraphs.S18.C005.P001: On the morning of day ten, the postcard was still on Eric's table. He had written to his sister himself: “We reached Höfn. My jacket got wet.” Alice saw only that line when he showed her a funny photograph of the boat; the rest remained his letter.
paragraphs.S18.C005.P002: The owner asked them to help check the sign in the morning. It turned out that returning the arrow to its former angle was not enough: a parked van blocked it from the other side. Alice walked the safe detour and drew the owner a diagram. She put it by the door until someone arrived to secure the sign. Eric did not claim the diagram as his. Alice did not turn the owner into an article character just because the conversation had gone well.
paragraphs.S18.C005.P003: They had breakfast with the whole group. Nick wanted to know whether anyone had seen the lit harbour at night, but Alice could answer him about the weather without reporting a kiss or its absence. During the day she walked through town, washed her scarf, and added two pages to her notes. Eric worked on the road and on his own things. Their evening did not take the next day away from either of them.
paragraphs.S18.C005.P004: Before bed on day ten, all four met in the hall while packing for the morning departure.

paragraphs.S18.C006.P000: Eric stopped beside Alice while Nick looked for the keys. “Would you be comfortable sitting beside me tomorrow?” he asked quietly. She said she would decide in the morning. He nodded and went to dry the thermos. In front of the others, yesterday's kiss was not repeated.

S18.C007.title: S18-S — after the evening without a kiss

paragraphs.S18.C007.P000: Eric handed Alice the scarf she had left by the diagram. “The song we argued about is in the car,” he said. She asked him to play it after the first stop. He wrote the title on his map.

paragraphs.S18.C008.P000: Eric pointed to the new detour on the diagram. “You noticed the mistake first yesterday. Thank you.” Alice took her notebook and said she would check one more address for the road in the morning. They went to their rooms.

S18.C010.title: Choice S18-C2 — How will Alice continue the conversation with Eric before the group leaves?

S18.C011.title: A. Ask about his grandfather's postcards

paragraphs.S18.C011.P000: Over breakfast, Alice asked Eric whether he still had his favourite postcard from his grandfather. He showed her a photograph of an old postage stamp on his phone. They talked about his family's travels; Alice did not try to turn the conversation into a confession.

S18.C012.title: B. Let him choose the music for the drive

paragraphs.S18.C012.P000: Alice asked Eric to choose the music for the first half-hour on the road. He searched for the right track for a long time, then settled on a song they had already listened to together. Alice suggested keeping it until they left—first everyone had to pack.
